speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when the accident occurred and how it looks now? Also, did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of the impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any loss of sensation or inability to move your right leg at the moment of the accident? Also, please tell me if the pain has radiated down your leg or into your foot since the injury occurred.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Right Hip X-Ray (AP and Frog-Leg views). REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the radiographs of the right hip and knee. Do you currently feel any numbness or tingling in the inner aspect of your right thigh?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray (AP and Frog-Leg views): No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip. No numbness or tingling reported in the inner aspect of the right thigh.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Hip Dislocation.

Based on the classic presentation of the right leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated following trauma, combined with severe groin pain, this is consistent with an anterior hip dislocation. The radiographs you requested should confirm the femoral head is displaced anteriorly and medial to the acetabulum.
